dream: The round rock rolled off the wide anchor because I forgot its name. The anchor fell onto the tired wedge, biting down like a hungry mouth. The wedge slid sideways, dragging the tall rock with it, tumbling off the card into a place called the Gaping Corner. There, the tall rock landed on the wide anchor again, just right, while the shadow stretched long to catch the slip. I pressed down on the nothing, trusting the lean to hold while the air turned thick as wet paper. Then the card hummed cool, and I woke up, wondering if the slip was still there.
